Chapter 10: Sustaining Change and Creating a Fulfilling Social Life.
So, you’ve made some real progress—now, how do you keep it going and actually build a social life that feels right for you?
Well, this last step is all about keeping those positive changes alive, and continuing to grow in ways that feel meaningful and authentic. Think of it like tending a garden. If you want things to flourish, you’ve got to keep watering, weeding, and nurturing what you’ve planted.
In the same way, maintaining your social confidence means giving ongoing attention to your own needs, your boundaries, and your goals.
Let’s talk about a few strategies that can really help:
First—regular self-check-ins. Every so often, just pause and reflect on your social experiences. What’s been rewarding? Where do you feel you could grow a little more?
Next, be willing to adjust your goals as life shifts. Things change—maybe you get a new job, move to a different city, or start a new relationship. It’s totally okay to update your goals to match whatever’s happening right now.
And don’t forget to celebrate your progress. Give yourself credit for how far you’ve come, even if you’re still on the journey. Each step forward matters.
Staying connected is huge, too. Keep seeking out relationships and spaces that actually support your growth, not just ones that drain your energy.
Here’s something to pay attention to: there’s no single definition of a “good” social life. Some people love big gatherings, while others feel most at home in quiet, one-on-one conversations. The point isn’t to fit into someone else’s idea of what social success looks like. The real goal is to shape a social life that fits your own values and brings you joy.
Picture this: maybe you used to dread parties, but now you realize you actually enjoy small get-togethers or group hikes, or maybe diving into a book club. By honoring your true preferences, you’ll build a social life that feels both comfortable and genuinely enriching.
And remember, sustaining change also means being gentle with yourself, especially when setbacks or anxiety pop up. Life is always shifting, and sometimes old habits sneak back during stressful times. When that happens, lean back into the basics—self-compassion, taking gradual steps, and reaching out for support when you need it.
That’s how you’ll keep growing, even when things get tough.
